title: Licensing costs driving 90 percent of VMware users to explore options: Survey
gist: A Rimini Street/Unisphere survey of 300 VMware-using organizations finds 90 percent exploring alternatives due to Broadcom's licensing costs, with 60 percent considering multi-hypervisor strategies, but operational complexity and skills gaps are the top barriers to migrating.

insights.claim: 90 percent of 300 surveyed VMware-using organizations are exploring alternatives due to higher licensing costs, and 54 percent cite Broadcom ending support for perpetual licenses.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Broadcom's pricing strategy is eroding customer loyalty, a long-term churn risk to VMware revenue.
insights.quote: 90 percent of participants in Rimini’s survey said they’re exploring VMware alternatives due to VMware’s higher licensing costs

insights.claim: Since Broadcom's takeover, VMware customers have reported cost increases as high as 1,000 percent, with many citing more modest hikes of 100-300 percent.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Price hikes of this scale explain Broadcom's VMware margin gains and the customer backlash.
insights.quote: customers have said that their VMware costs increased by as much as 1,000 percent

insights.claim: The survey sponsor Rimini Street sells third-party support for VMware, giving it an incentive to portray users as struggling, though the survey was run by Unisphere Research and aligns with other reports.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Read survey numbers with sponsor bias in mind.
insights.quote: there’s an incentive for Rimini to portray VMware users as experiencing obstacles.

insights.claim: The most cited barriers to moving off VMware are operational complexity (40%), multi-vendor management (38%), securing an increased attack surface (37%), and team skills requirements (37%).
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Switching costs blunt the exodus, giving Broadcom pricing power despite customer anger.
insights.quote: operational complexity (named by 40 percent of respondents), multi-vendor management challenges (38 percent)

insights.claim: 48 percent of respondents are not planning to move any assets to VMware Cloud Foundation, Broadcom's hybrid cloud platform.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Weak uptake of VCF limits Broadcom's upsell strategy.
insights.quote: 48 percent of respondents aren’t planning to move any of their assets to VMware’s hybrid cloud platform, Cloud Foundation.

insights.claim: 60 percent of organizations are considering a multi-hypervisor strategy and 47 percent favor hybrid environments mixing hypervisors and containers.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Beneficiaries include alternative hypervisor and container platform vendors.
insights.quote: 60 percent of the organizations it surveyed are considering a multi-hypervisor strategy

insights.claim: Gartner predicts 55 percent of enterprises will run proofs of concept for alternative distributed hybrid infrastructure products to replace VMware deployments by 2029, up from 25 percent in 2026.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Signals a multi-year, gradual erosion of VMware's installed base rather than a sudden exit.
insights.quote: which is an increase from 25 percent in 2026.

insights.claim: Gartner's Tony Harvey says many clients treat Broadcom's acquisition as a wake-up call about single-vendor dependence and seek more diversity in on-premises environments.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Vendor-concentration aversion is a durable tailwind for VMware competitors.
insights.quote: a wake-up call to how dependent they had become on a single vendor
